origin.description: Skewness of a statistic from its empirical influence values.

arguments.name: L
arguments.text: Empirical influence values of a statistic, usually from empinf.

arguments.name: strata
arguments.text: Numeric vector or factor saying which observations belong to which stratum. NULL puts every observation in one stratum.

origin.details: The estimate adds, over strata, sum(L_i^3) / n_s^3, where n_s is the number of observations in that stratum. Distinct values are grouped together. A missing stratum label makes the estimate missing.
origin.example:
#  To estimate the skewness of the ratio of means for the city data.
ratio <- function(d, w) sum(d$x * w)/sum(d$u * w)
k3.linear(empinf(data = city, statistic = ratio))

translation.description: Skewness of a statistic from its empirical influence values.

arguments.name: L
arguments.text: Empirical influence values of a statistic.

arguments.name: strata
arguments.text: Numeric vector or list of labels saying which observations belong to which stratum. None puts every observation in one stratum. A missing label makes the result NaN.

translation.details: The estimate adds, over strata, sum(L_i^3) / n_s^3, where n_s is the number of observations in that stratum. Equal values form one stratum. A missing stratum label makes the result NaN.
